questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Primary it was the nature, and an Erasmus was perfect. I wanted to experience the life next to the fjords and also see how it is to live in a more northern country than Denmark. I loved to see how technology is evolved in Norway. It was also interesting how the courses are different to Denmark and how its they teach the subjects differently. I chose Bergen because I always wanted to visit it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The University of Bergen gave a perfect experience for a student. It provided me with an accommodation, where I had honestly the easiest experience of finding an apartment/ room. The University helped with EVERYTHING. Also with helping to get into the Norwegian culture and how to find friends with volunteering or clubs at the University. It was the perfect place to go anytime and the employees were always really helpful.  The introduction week helped to find friends, I enjoyed during my whole Erasmus time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a responsible person which helped me with all the organizational stuff for the Erasmus. And also I received help in the introduction courses, where they gave you an overview of how to apply for courses or how to live in Bergen /Norway in general. They did an excellent job in making you feel like home, or in making you feel welcomed by everyone.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, just follow the introduction of the University and it will be fine. They provide everything and ensure for the international students that they receive a room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is a small city, so don't worry where you live you don't take so much time to university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to register from a course catalog in Soknabsweb and they provided me with a detailed description of the procedure

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could ask the responsible Erasmus person, and you receive an email with the details. There is also the website.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was good, just some of the classes where overlapping so it was complicated to attend the one I wanted to take.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be aware that a lot of the courses overlap. And if you are not sure about anything just ask!! and apply very soon for the Norwegian course, the deadline ends early.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Introduction. to Cognitive Science of BA ( 1 year), Natural Resource Management ( MA 1. year), Software Specification (MA 1. year ) each of them have 10 ECTS

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Yes and no. The Cognitive Science course it is similar, but the Natural Resource Management course was a only online course and the Software Specification course was like a small UCPH Master course, and my favourite one.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to Cognitive Science, Natural Resource Management, Software Specification

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just take the Norwegian Intro course/ or the language course, I would have love to take it. But all the courses at UIB are good quality.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The travels and the high supermarket prices, be aware that Norway is really expensive when you consider basics like vegetables.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The groceries were more expensive and the alcohol. Going out is similar to Copenhagen ( except alcohol ) and also going to a coffee is similar to Copenhagen prices. The rent is less expensive then in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have a gym membership where a swimming pool and a bouldering hall is included and all kind of group classes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I went to yoga, afrobeat, swimming and to the gym. I helped in Kvarteret( a student cafe from Bergen ) and I went to the social activities of the faculty of informatics.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Volunteering and sports are good ideas. I would recommend a Damen gym membership and volunteering at one of the many student clubs in Bergen.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend to hike one of the 7 mountains, go to Bryggen, take cruise tour and try the whale salami. Bergen is rainy so take the raincoat. But the city is absolutely worth a visit and it's absolutely beautiful. Hiking on one mountain is a must for a Norwegian experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: The Norwegians are a little reserved like the danish people, but with the help of the introduction week it was doable to create a connection with Norwegians. The University helped us to arrive and guided us through the first couple of weeks, so I never felt really alone in the things I had to do. The international office helped with the documents and the student advisor could help with any type of questions. The University taught us in the beginning some thing about the Norwegian culture and made us aware of the differences.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Attend the social clubs, in informatics they do a lot of social events and just talk to them. They will gladly help you with anything. It is hard to find a Norwegian friend, but just ask them to drink a beer and they would love to hang out with you. A drunk Norwegian can become your best friend. It takes time and I was happy to find one Norwegian friend, but this is not normal so don't put so much pressure, be nice, try to ask them if they join you for a hike or a beer and you will be fine. When you hike with a Norwegian be aware that they hike very fast.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: To Danes there are not so many cultural differences. Finding Norwegian friends is a little challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I like a lot the hiking culture and that if you find a Norwegian friend they are very funny and always interesting to be around.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Take a rain jacket, try to get to know a person from Bergen and you will fall in love with bergen

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the Norwegian course early!! and Take a lot for the Rain. Don't miss the introduction week, because there you meet a lot of nice people, that can be your friends. And please just ask anyone at the University if you have questions, because they are really helpful.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: My friends and also to have the experience to live in a norwegian city, which I would have never dreamed about. I loved every day, because I also learned so much about myself in this experience

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Dealing with the 1 hour more of darkness, and the rain and being far away from my friends was hard. But after 2 months I had very good friends in Bergen and they made the rain and the darkness beautiful and they helped me to enjoy the city more.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
